OCCURRENCE. — Acontheus inarmatus is a rare middle Cambrian taxon, reported from southeastern Canada, eastern Newfoundland, in the Paradoxides davidis Zone (Hutchinson 1962). It has further been documented from Germany (Sdzuy 2000).

Distribution. Map (Fig. 45). Known from Argentina, where it has been recorded from Buenos Aires; Chaco; Corrientes; Formosa; Misiones; Salta; Santa Fe; Santiago del Estero. New records: Entre Ríos; Córdoba. Host plant. The only known host plant is Medicago sativa (Bosq, 1942; Hayward, 1960; Di Iorio, 2004).
Occurrence. Lower Eocene (lower Ypresian) of Spilecco Hill near Bolca, north-eastern Italy.
